Run an asynchronous function only once

Source: R/async_once.R
async_once.Rd

Asynchronous version of once(), for functions that return a promise. The first call's resolved value is kept and every later call returns a promise of it, ignoring its arguments. Calls made while the first is still running share its promise. A rejection stores nothing, so the next call tries again. Needs the promises package.

Usage

async_once(f)

Arguments

f

The function to decorate. Usually supplied by %@% rather than directly.

Value

A decorator. The decorated function returns a promise.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
setup := async_once %@% function() {
  cat("setting up\n")
  promises::promise_resolve(42)
}
promises::then(setup(), print)
promises::then(setup(), print) # no second "setting up"
while (!later::loop_empty()) later::run_now(0.05)
} # }
